sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca śrūyatāṃ pṛthivīpāla kṣaratīdaṃ yathā jagat yan na kṣarati pūrveṇa yāvat kālena cāpy atha
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Hear, O lord of the earth, how this world perishes, and what it is that does not perish, and through how vast a span of time it endures.

sanskrit: yugaṃ dvādaśasāhasraṃ kalpaṃ viddhi caturguṇam daśakalpaśatāvṛttaṃ tad ahar brāhmam ucyate rātriś caitāvatī rājan yasyānte pratibudhyate
english: Know that an age is twelve thousand years, and a kalpa four times that; a thousand kalpas turning round make up what is called the Day of Brahmā, and the Night, O king, is of equal length—at whose end He awakens.

sanskrit: sṛjaty anantakarmāṇaṃ mahāntaṃ bhūtam agrajam mūrtimantam amūrtātmā viśvaṃ śaṃbhuḥ svayaṃbhuvaḥ aṇimā laghimā prāptir īśānaṃ jyotir avyayam
english: Then the formless Self, Śambhu, the source of all good, brings forth the Great One, the firstborn being of endless action, embodied and all-pervading—endowed with the powers of minuteness, lightness, and attainment, the lordly, imperishable Light.

sanskrit: sarvataḥpāṇipādāntaṃ sarvatokṣiśiromukham sarvataḥśrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
english: With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces turned in every direction, with ears in every quarter, it stands enveloping all things in the world.

sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbho bhagavān eṣa buddhir iti smṛtaḥ mahān iti ca yogeṣu viriñca iti cāpy uta
english: This blessed one is Hiraṇyagarbha; he is remembered as Intellect (buddhi), and among the Yogins as the Great (mahat), and likewise as Viriñca.

sanskrit: sāṃkhye ca paṭhyate śāstre nāmabhir bahudhātmakaḥ vicitrarūpo viśvātmā ekākṣara iti smṛtaḥ
english: In the Sāṃkhya treatise too he is recited under many names, manifold in nature, varied in form, the Soul of the Universe, remembered as the One Imperishable Syllable.

sanskrit: vṛtaṃ naikātmakaṃ yena kṛtsnaṃ trailokyam ātmanā tathaiva bahurūpatvād viśvarūpa iti smṛtaḥ
english: Since by him the whole threefold world, manifold in essence, is enveloped through his own self, and because of his many forms, he is remembered as the All-formed (Viśvarūpa).

sanskrit: eṣa vai vikriyāpannaḥ sṛjaty ātmānam ātmanā ahaṃkāraṃ mahātejāḥ prajāpatim ahaṃkṛtam
english: This one, having undergone transformation, brings forth from himself by himself the Ego-principle (ahaṃkāra)—he of great splendor begets the self-conscious Lord of Creatures.

sanskrit: avyaktād vyaktam utpannaṃ vidyāsargaṃ vadanti tam mahāntaṃ cāpy ahaṃkāram avidyāsargam eva ca
english: From the Unmanifest the Manifest arises; this they call the creation born of Knowledge—namely the Great One; while the Ego-principle they call the creation born of Ignorance.

sanskrit: avidhiś ca vidhiś caiva samutpannau tathaikataḥ vidyāvidyeti vikhyāte śrutiśāstrārthacintakaiḥ
english: The lawless and the lawful alike arose together from one source; they are proclaimed as Knowledge and Ignorance by those who ponder the meaning of scripture and treatise.

sanskrit: bhūtasargam ahaṃkārāt tṛtīyaṃ viddhi pārthiva ahaṃkāreṣu bhūteṣu caturthaṃ viddhi vaikṛtam
english: Know, O son of Pṛthā, that the creation of the elements from the Ego-principle is the third; and within the Ego and the elements know the fourth, the modified creation.

sanskrit: vāyur jyotir athākāśam āpo 'tha pṛthivī tathā śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhas tathaiva ca
english: Air, fire, then ether, water, and earth likewise; sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as well.

sanskrit: evaṃ yugapad utpannaṃ daśavargam asaṃśayam pañcamaṃ viddhi rājendra bhautikaṃ sargam arthavat
english: Thus this group of ten arose all at once, beyond doubt; know it, O king of kings, as the fifth, the elemental creation, full of purpose.

sanskrit: śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā ghrāṇam eva ca pañcamam vāk ca hastau ca pādau ca pāyur meḍhraṃ tathaiva ca
english: Ear, skin, the two eyes, tongue, and smell as the fifth; and speech, the two hands, the two feet, the anus, and the organ of generation as well—

sanskrit: buddhīndriyāṇi caitāni tathā karmendriyāṇi ca saṃbhūtānīha yugapan manasā saha pārthiva
english: these are the organs of perception and the organs of action; they all came into being here at once, together with the mind, O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: eṣā tattvacaturviṃśā sarvākṛtiṣu vartate yāṃ jñātvā nābhiśocanti brāhmaṇās tattvadarśinaḥ
english: This set of twenty-four principles abides in all forms; knowing which, the Brāhmaṇas who perceive truth grieve no more.

sanskrit: etad dehaṃ samākhyātaṃ trailokye sarvadehiṣu veditavyaṃ naraśreṣṭha sadevanaradānave
english: This is declared to be the body in all embodied beings throughout the three worlds; it is to be understood so, O best of men, among gods, men, and Dānavas alike,

sanskrit: sayakṣabhūtagandharve sakiṃnaramahorage sacāraṇapiśāce vai sadevarṣiniśācare
english: among Yakṣas, spirits, and Gandharvas, among Kiṃnaras and great serpents, among Cāraṇas and Piśācas, among celestial sages and night-roaming demons,

sanskrit: sadaṃśakīṭamaśake sapūtikṛmimūṣake śuni śvapāke vaiṇeye sacaṇḍāle sapulkase
english: among gnats, insects, and mosquitoes, among foul worms and mice, in the dog and the dog-cooker, the basket-weaver, the Caṇḍāla, and the Pulkasa,

sanskrit: hastyaśvakharaśārdūle savṛkṣe gavi caiva ha yac ca mūrtimayaṃ kiṃ cit sarvatraitan nidarśanam
english: in elephant, horse, ass, and tiger, in tree and in cow as well—whatever possesses bodily form anywhere, this same teaching applies.

sanskrit: jale bhuvi tathākāśe nānyatreti viniścayaḥ sthānaṃ dehavatām asti ity evam anuśuśruma
english: In water, on earth, and in the sky—nowhere else: such is the settled conclusion that there is an abode for embodied beings; thus have we heard it handed down.

sanskrit: kṛtsnam etāvatas tāta kṣarate vyaktasaṃjñakam ahany ahani bhūtātmā tataḥ kṣara iti smṛtaḥ
english: All of this much, my son, that bears the name of the Manifest, perishes; day after day the elemental self decays, and therefore it is remembered as the Perishable (kṣara).

sanskrit: etad akṣaram ity uktaṃ kṣaratīdaṃ yathā jagat jagan mohātmakaṃ prāhur avyaktaṃ vyaktasaṃjñakam
english: This too has been called Imperishable—even as this world perishes; they declare the world, whose essence is delusion, to be the Unmanifest bearing the name of the Manifest.

sanskrit: mahāṃś caivāgrajo nityam etat kṣaranidarśanam kathitaṃ te mahārāja yasmān nāvartate punaḥ
english: The Great One too, the firstborn, is eternal: this is the exposition of the Perishable, told to you, O great king—from which one does not return again.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśatimo viṣṇur nistattvas tattvasaṃjñakaḥ tattvasaṃśrayaṇād etat tattvam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: The twenty-fifth is Viṣṇu, beyond the principles yet named a principle; because it is the refuge of the principles, the wise call it the True (tattva).

sanskrit: yad amūrty asṛjad vyaktaṃ tat tan mūrty adhitiṣṭhati caturviṃśatimo vyakto hy amūrtaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ
english: Whatever the formless created as the Manifest, that very form it presides over; the twenty-fourth is the Manifest, while the formless is the twenty-fifth.

sanskrit: sa eva hṛdi sarvāsu mūrtiṣv ātiṣṭhate ''tmavān cetayaṃś cetano nityaḥ sarvamūrtir amūrtimān
english: That very Self abides in the heart within all forms—the conscious one, ever giving consciousness, eternal, taking on all forms yet itself formless.

sanskrit: sargapralayadharmiṇyā asargapralayātmakaḥ gocare vartate nityaṃ nirguṇo guṇasaṃjñakaḥ
english: Subject to a Nature whose law is creation and dissolution, it is itself without creation or dissolution; it ever ranges within her domain, free of the qualities yet called by their name.

sanskrit: evam eṣa mahān ātmā sargapralayakovidaḥ vikurvāṇaḥ prakṛtimān abhimanyaty abuddhimān
english: Thus this Great Soul, skilled in creation and dissolution, undergoing transformation and possessed of Nature, in its want of wisdom takes these to be its own.

sanskrit: tamaḥsattvarajoyuktas tāsu tāsv iha yoniṣu līyate 'pratibuddhatvād abuddhajanasevanāt
english: Yoked to darkness, goodness, and passion, it dissolves into one womb after another here below, through its failure to awaken and its keeping company with the unawakened.

sanskrit: sahavāso nivāsātmā nānyo 'ham iti manyate yo 'haṃ so 'ham iti hy uktvā guṇān anu nivartate
english: Its very nature being to dwell in fellowship, it thinks, 'I am no other than this'; and saying, 'What I am, that I am,' it turns and follows after the qualities.

sanskrit: tamasā tāmasān bhāvān vividhān pratipadyate rajasā rājasāṃś caiva sāttvikān sattvasaṃśrayāt
english: Through darkness it attains to manifold states marked by darkness, through passion to those marked by passion, and through resort to goodness to those that are good.

sanskrit: śuklalohitakṛṣṇāni rūpāṇy etāni trīṇi tu sarvāṇy etāni rūpāṇi jānīhi prākṛtāni vai
english: White, red, and black—these are the three colors; know that all these colors belong to Nature.

sanskrit: tāmasā nirayaṃ yānti rājasā mānuṣāṃs tathā sāttvikā devalokāya gacchanti sukhabhāginaḥ
english: Those of darkness go to hell, those of passion to the human estate, while the partakers of goodness, sharing in happiness, go to the world of the gods.

sanskrit: niṣkaivalyena pāpena tiryagyonim avāpnuyāt puṇyapāpena mānuṣyaṃ puṇyenaikena devatāḥ
english: By unmixed sin one reaches the animal womb, by merit and sin together the human state, and by merit alone the rank of the gods.

sanskrit: evam avyaktaviṣayaṃ kṣaram āhur manīṣiṇaḥ pañcaviṃśatimo yo 'yaṃ jñānād eva pravartate
english: Thus the wise call that whose sphere is the Unmanifest the Perishable; but this twenty-fifth one comes forth into action through knowledge alone.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca evam apratibuddhatvād abuddham anuvartate dehād dehasahasrāṇi tathā samabhipadyate
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Thus, through its failure to awaken, the unawakened one follows along, and so passes from one body into thousands of bodies.

sanskrit: tiryagyonisahasreṣu kadā cid devatāsv api upapadyati saṃyogād guṇaiḥ saha guṇakṣayāt
english: Now into thousands of animal wombs, now even among the gods, it is born—through its conjunction with the qualities and, again, through the wasting of those qualities.

sanskrit: mānuṣatvād divaṃ yāti divo mānuṣyam eva ca mānuṣyān nirayasthānam ānantyaṃ pratipadyate
english: From manhood it goes to heaven, and from heaven back to manhood; from manhood it attains the place of hell, in endless succession.

sanskrit: kośakāro yathātmānaṃ kīṭaḥ samanurundhati sūtratantuguṇair nityaṃ tathāyam aguṇo guṇaiḥ
english: As the cocoon-spinning worm binds itself fast forever with the threads and strands it spins, so does this one, though itself qualityless, bind itself with the qualities.

sanskrit: dvaṃdvam eti ca nirdvaṃdvas tāsu tāsv iha yoniṣu śīrṣaroge 'kṣiroge ca dantaśūle galagrahe
english: Though beyond all pairs of opposites, it meets with them in womb after womb here below—in headache and eye-disease, in toothache and quinsy,

sanskrit: jalodare 'rśasāṃ roge jvaragaṇḍaviṣūcike śvitre kuṣṭhe 'gnidāhe ca sidhmāpasmārayor api
english: in dropsy and the disease of piles, in fever, swellings, and cholera, in leucoderma, leprosy, and burning fever, and in skin-eruption and epilepsy too,

sanskrit: yāni cānyāni dvaṃdvāni prākṛtāni śarīriṣu utpadyante vicitrāṇi tāny eṣo 'py abhimanyate abhimanyaty abhīmānāt tathaiva sukṛtāny api
english: and whatever other manifold pairs of opposites, born of Nature, arise in embodied beings—these too this one claims as its own; out of conceit it claims them, and its good deeds likewise.

sanskrit: ekavāsāś ca durvāsāḥ śāyī nityam adhas tathā maṇḍūkaśāyī ca tathā vīrāsanagatas tathā
english: Clad in a single garment, or ill-clad; sleeping ever upon the bare ground; lying crouched like a frog; or seated in the hero's posture;

sanskrit: cīradhāraṇam ākāśe śayanaṃ sthānam eva ca iṣṭakāprastare caiva kaṇṭakaprastare tathā
english: wearing rags; sleeping or standing under the open sky; lying upon a bed of bricks, or upon a bed of thorns;

sanskrit: bhasmaprastaraśāyī ca bhūmiśayyānulepanaḥ vīrasthānāmbupaṅke ca śayanaṃ phalakeṣu ca
english: lying upon a bed of ashes; sleeping on bare earth and smearing the body; resting in the hero's stance, in water, or in mire, or upon wooden planks;

sanskrit: vividhāsu ca śayyāsu phalagṛddhyānvito 'phalaḥ muñjamekhalanagnatvaṃ kṣaumakṛṣṇājināni ca
english: upon couches of many kinds—craving reward yet itself reaping none; girt with the muñja-grass cord or going naked, clad in linen or in black antelope-skins;

sanskrit: śāṇīvālaparīdhāno vyāghracarmaparicchadaḥ siṃhacarmaparīdhānaḥ paṭṭavāsās tathaiva ca
english: wrapped in hempen cloth, covered with a tiger's hide, draped in a lion's skin, or clothed in fine silk;

sanskrit: kīṭakāvasanaś caiva cīravāsās tathaiva ca vastrāṇi cānyāni bahūny abhimanyaty abuddhimān
english: clad in cocoon-silk or dressed in rags—and many other garments besides does the unwise one claim as its own.

sanskrit: bhojanāni vicitrāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca ekavastrāntarāśitvam ekakālikabhojanam
english: Manifold foods and jewels of many kinds; eating with but a single cloth between, and taking food but once a day;

sanskrit: caturthāṣṭamakālaś ca ṣaṣṭhakālika eva ca ṣaḍrātrabhojanaś caiva tathaivāṣṭāhabhojanaḥ
english: eating at every fourth or eighth watch, or at every sixth meal-time; breaking fast only after six nights, or likewise only after eight days;

sanskrit: saptarātradaśāhāro dvādaśāhāra eva ca māsopavāsī mūlāśī phalāhāras tathaiva ca
english: eating once in seven nights or once in ten days, or even once in twelve; fasting a whole month; living on roots, or living on fruits;

sanskrit: vāyubhakṣo 'mbupiṇyākagomayādana eva ca gomūtrabhojanaś caiva śākapuṣpāda eva ca
english: feeding on air, or on water, oil-cake, and cow-dung; drinking cow's urine; eating herbs and flowers;

sanskrit: śaivālabhojanaś caiva tathācāmena vartayan vartayañ śīrṇaparṇaiś ca prakīrṇaphalabhojanaḥ
english: living on water-moss, or subsisting on rice-water; sustaining itself on withered leaves, or eating only fruits that have fallen of themselves;

sanskrit: vividhāni ca kṛcchrāṇi sevate sukhakāṅkṣayā cāndrāyaṇāni vidhival liṅgāni vividhāni ca
english: it practices manifold austere penances in its longing for happiness—the moon-fasts duly performed, and the various outward marks of asceticism;

sanskrit: cāturāśramyapanthānam āśrayaty āśramān api upāsīnaś ca pāṣaṇḍān guhāḥ śailāṃs tathaiva ca
english: it resorts to the path of the four orders of life and to the hermitages, attending upon heretics, dwelling in caves and upon mountains as well,

sanskrit: viviktāś ca śilāchāyās tathā prasravaṇāni ca vividhāni ca japyāni vividhāni vratāni ca
english: in lonely places, in the shade of rocks, and beside the springs; with manifold prayers murmured low and manifold vows;

sanskrit: niyamān suvicitrāṃś ca vividhāni tapāṃsi ca yajñāṃś ca vividhākārān vidhīṃś ca vividhāṃs tathā
english: with most varied observances and austerities of many kinds, with sacrifices of many forms and rites of many sorts;

sanskrit: vaṇikpathaṃ dvijakṣatraṃ vaiśyaśūdraṃ tathaiva ca dānaṃ ca vividhākāraṃ dīnāndhakṛpaṇeṣv api
english: the trader's calling, the estates of Brāhmaṇa and Kṣatriya, of Vaiśya and Śūdra alike, and charity of many kinds, even to the poor, the blind, and the wretched—

sanskrit: abhimanyaty asaṃbodhāt tathaiva trividhān guṇān sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva dharmārthau kāma eva ca prakṛtyātmānam evātmā evaṃ pravibhajaty uta
english: all this it claims as its own through want of true understanding; and so too the threefold qualities—goodness, passion, and darkness—and righteousness, wealth, and desire. Thus does the self, which is but Nature, divide up its own self in this way.

sanskrit: svadhākāravaṣaṭkārau svāhākāranamaskriyāḥ yājanādhyāpanaṃ dānaṃ tathaivāhuḥ pratigraham yajanādhyayane caiva yac cānyad api kiṃ cana
english: The cries of svadhā and vaṣaṭ, of svāhā and the acts of homage; officiating at sacrifices and teaching, giving and—so they say—receiving gifts, sacrificing and studying, and whatever else there is besides—

sanskrit: janmamṛtyuvivāde ca tathā viśasane 'pi ca śubhāśubhamayaṃ sarvam etad āhuḥ kriyāpatham
english: and in birth and death, in dispute, and in slaughter too—all this, made up of good and evil, they call the path of action.

sanskrit: prakṛtiḥ kurute devī mahāpralayam eva ca divasānte guṇān etān abhyetyaiko 'vatiṣṭhati
english: It is Nature, the goddess, who brings about the great dissolution as well; at the day's end she gathers in these qualities, and the One alone abides.

sanskrit: raśmijālam ivādityas tatkālena niyacchati evam eṣo 'sakṛt sarvaṃ krīḍārtham abhimanyate
english: As the sun draws in its net of rays at the appointed time, so does this one, again and again, claim all things as its own for the sake of sport.

sanskrit: ātmarūpaguṇān etān vividhān hṛdayapriyān evam eva vikurvāṇaḥ sargapralayakarmaṇī
english: These manifold qualities, in the likeness of its own self and dear to its heart, it transforms in just this way, performing the works of creation and dissolution.

sanskrit: kriyākriyā pathe raktas triguṇas triguṇātigaḥ kriyākriyāpathopetas tathā tad iti manyate
english: Attached to the path of action and inaction, it becomes endowed with the three qualities though it transcends them; engaged upon the path of action and inaction, it thinks, 'This is indeed I.'

sanskrit: evaṃ dvaṃdvāny athaitāni vartante mama nityaśaḥ mamaivaitāni jāyante bādhante tāni mām iti
english: It thinks: 'Thus these pairs of opposites are ever present with me; these arise for me alone, and these afflict me.'

sanskrit: nistartavyāny athaitāni sarvāṇīti narādhipa manyate 'yaṃ hy abuddhitvāt tathaiva sukṛtāny api
english: 'And all these are to be surmounted by me'—so it thinks, O lord of men, in its want of wisdom; and it thinks the like of its good deeds as well.

sanskrit: bhoktavyāni mayaitāni devalokagatena vai ihaiva cainaṃ bhokṣyāmi śubhāśubhaphalodayam
english: 'These fruits are to be enjoyed by me when I have gone to the world of the gods; and here itself I shall enjoy this harvest of good and evil that ripens.'

sanskrit: sukham eva ca kartavyaṃ sakṛt kṛtvā sukhaṃ mama yāvadantaṃ ca me saukhyaṃ jātyāṃ jātyāṃ bhaviṣyati
english: 'And happiness alone is to be pursued; once I have secured my happiness, my felicity shall endure to the very end, birth after birth.'

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati ca me duḥkhaṃ kṛtenehāpy anantakam mahad duḥkhaṃ hi mānuṣyaṃ niraye cāpi majjanam
english: 'Yet sorrow without end shall also be mine here, through what I have done; for the human state is great suffering, and so too is the plunge into hell.'

sanskrit: nirayāc cāpi mānuṣyaṃ kālenaiṣyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ manuṣyatvāc ca devatvaṃ devatvāt pauruṣaṃ punaḥ manuṣyatvāc ca nirayaṃ paryāyeṇopagacchati
english: 'And from hell I shall in time come again to the human state.' From manhood to godhood, from godhood back to manhood, and from manhood to hell it passes by turns.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ vetti vai nityaṃ nirātmātmaguṇair vṛtaḥ tena devamanuṣyeṣu niraye copapadyate
english: He who thinks thus, forever selfless yet enveloped by the qualities of the self, by reason of that is born again among gods and men and in hell.

sanskrit: mamatvenāvṛto nityaṃ tatraiva parivartate sargakoṭisahasrāṇi maraṇāntāsu mūrtiṣu
english: Forever wrapped in the sense of 'mine,' it revolves there alone, through thousands upon millions of creations, in forms that all end in death.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ kurute karma śubhāśubhaphalātmakam sa eva phalam aśnāti triṣu lokeṣu mūrtimān
english: Whoever performs action whose nature is fruit good and evil, he himself, embodied, eats of that fruit throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: prakṛtiḥ kurute karma śubhāśubhaphalātmakam prakṛtiś ca tad aśnāti triṣu lokeṣu kāmagā
english: It is Nature that performs the action whose nature is fruit good and evil, and it is Nature, roaming where she wills, that eats of it throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: tiryagyonau manuṣyatve devaloke tathaiva ca trīṇi sthānāni caitāni jānīyāt prākṛtāni ha
english: In the animal womb, in the human state, and likewise in the world of the gods—these three stations one should know to belong to Nature.

sanskrit: aliṅgāṃ prakṛtiṃ tv āhur liṅgair anumimīmahe tathaiva pauruṣaṃ liṅgam anumānād dhi paśyati
english: Nature they declare to be without distinguishing mark, yet by its marks we infer it; and the mark of the Spirit too one perceives only by inference.

sanskrit: sa liṅgāntaram āsādya prākṛtaṃ liṅgam avraṇam vraṇadvārāṇy adhiṣṭhāya karmāṇy ātmani manyate
english: Having taken on another mark—the wound-free mark of Nature—and presiding over the gateways of the wounds, it imagines the actions to be in the self.

sanskrit: śrotrādīni tu sarvāṇi pañca karmendriyāṇi ca vāg ādīni pravartante guṇeṣv eva guṇaiḥ saha aham etāni vai kurvan mamaitānīndriyāṇi ca
english: All the organs beginning with the ear, and the five organs of action beginning with speech, function only amid the qualities, together with the qualities; yet it thinks, 'It is I who do these, and these senses are mine.'
